newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Oversupply fears push Seoul shares to lower end.
newsitem.headline: Oversupply fears push Seoul shares to lower end.

text.p: Shares ended below the psychologically important support level of 750 on Monday on concerns about an oversuppy of shares in November, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed at a provisional 747.43, down 18.30 points, or 2.39 percent.
Declining shares led gainers by seven to one.
"The main trigger for the current plunge is the aggravated imbalance between supply and demand," said Hur Gyung-shik of Samsung Securities.
"There is a sizeable amount of stock supply coming on-stream in November, adding to the underlying uncertain economic picture."

The new stock supply in November is estimated at more than 1.1 trillion won, according to brokers. Rights and bonus issues alone is seen adding about 650 billion won, while the government has announced plans to sell 13.3 million shares, valued at 500 billion won, of the state-backed Korea Telecom.
Loans for margin trading are approaching three trillion won, while customer deposits have declined to around 2.5 trillion, brokers said.
Between 500-900 billion won worth of the loans will have to be repaid this month, they added.
The index has fallen about 24 percent from its 1996 high of 986.84 reached in May.

The mid-term outlook for the market looked gloomy, Hur said. "The important support line of 750 collapsed without any noticeable resistance, so the outlook is uncertain," he said. "In the worst case scenario, the KOSPI could fall below 700."
Small-cap shares, which had led recent rises, were the worst hit by selling. Choong Wae Pharmacy lost 2,300 won to its lower limit of 36,700. Young Poong Mining shed 3,000 won to 58,000.
Blue chips also fell. Samsung Electronics lost 2,100 won to 59,200 and Dacom 3,500 won to 113,000.
December futures fell 3.40 points to 78.60, while the KOSPI 200 index shed 1.86 points to 77.95.

Brokers said there was the possibility of a limited technical rebound on Tuesday, but that without a change in fundamentals, the market looked set on a downward course for the time being. The composit index was later revised to 747.42.
